attribs.name: repeating_inventory_-NzEf3xdr3u0OUEpEaXJ_itemcontent
attribs.current:
This copper amulet contains tiny interlocking gears and is powered by magic from Mechanus, a plane of clockwork predictability. A creature that puts an ear to the amulet can hear faint ticking and whirring noises coming from within.

When you make an attack roll while wearing the amulet, you can forgo rolling the d20 to get a 10 on the die. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

attribs.name: repeating_inventory_-NzEf4SxGyoAQ8d9dTNU_itemcontent
attribs.current:
This striking satin jacket allows you to make the most of your dying moments. When you drop to 0 hit points while wearing this doublet, you do not fall unconscious. Instead, you are incapacitated and your speed becomes 0, but you can speak and communicate.

You make death saving throws as normal, but if you roll a 1 on the d20, you swoon with a loud gasp and die instantly.

attribs.name: repeating_inventory_-NzEf55HzbkSPduqIcHO_itemcontent
attribs.current:
While you wear this pendant, you stabilize whenever you are dying at the start of your turn. In addition, whenever you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, double the number of hit points it restores.

attribs.name: repeating_inventory_-NzEf5VQtC0jotVux2zC_itemcontent
attribs.current:
This wand has 3 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges and target a humanoid you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must succeed on a DC 10 Charisma saving throw or be forced to scowl for 1 minute.

The wand regains all expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the wand transforms into a wand of smiles.

attribs.name: repeating_inventory_-NzEf5ucgtZBO6VWIFPZ_itemcontent
attribs.current:
While you wear these boots, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You can use the boots to fly for up to 4 hours, all at once or in several shorter flights, each one using a minimum of 1 minute from the duration. If you are flying when the duration expires, you descend at a rate of 30 feet per round until you land.

The boots regain 2 hours of flying capability for every 12 hours they aren't in use.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-NzEu40DQ6LqQYXnXCfw_description
attribs.current: Your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-NzEvBQ36l5QHPy58blT_description
attribs.current: Your unexpected good fortune is reflected by a minor boon. You gain the Lucky, Magic Initiate, or Skilled feat (your choice). Your choice of feat reflects the transformation that changed your life. An encounter with a genie who gave you three wishes might have resulted in magical powers represented by Magic Initiate. If you paid off all your family debts with a fortuitous round of three-dragon ante, you might be Lucky instead. Alternatively, you could use the Skilled feat to reflect whatever trial you endured to secure your new destiny and to model the knowledge and abilities imparted to you by whatever force transformed your life.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-NzEvZ5lQ2v9TYLUH6Kf_description
attribs.current:
You have inexplicable luck that seems to kick in at just the right moment.
You have 3 luck points. Whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can spend one luck point to roll an additional d20. You can choose to spend one of your luck points after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You choose which of the d20s is used for the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

You can also spend one luck point when an attack roll is made against you. Roll a d20, and then choose whether the attack uses the attacker's roll or yours. If more than one creature spends a luck point to influence the outcome of a roll, the points cancel each other out; no additional dice are rolled.

You regain your expended luck points when you finish a long rest.

attribs.current:
You have a mind for tactics and getting the upper hand on and off the battlefield. Beginning at 2nd level, whenever you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself towards success.

Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-NzF1rmxAG0Snc5nRyyy_description

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-NzF3S6GbX0DTcTwBE-V_description
attribs.current:
Starting at 3rd level, you gain the ability to adopt elemental stances, each offering unique enhancements to your attacks. When you make a weapon attack, you may choose one of your stances to activate it, adding the effects from the stance if it hits. Repeated attacks made with the same stance grants additional effects stacking based on the number of successful attacks made. Switching stances resets the stacks to 0.

The saving throw DC for stance effects is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (whichever is higher) = 18.

Select two stances initially, you may choose an additional stance when you reach the 7th, 10th and 15th level in this class.

Blaze Reprisal Stance
Solar Flare Stance
Void Embrace Stance
Glacial Guard Stance

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-NzF4e48zZmynC0CJtAr_description
attribs.current:
At 7th level, you gain the ability to combine your chosen melee weapon and firearm into a singular, powerful weapon: the Elemental Gunblade. This fusion requires a ritual that spans a day and a night, during which you must channel elemental energies into the weapons, binding them with your own spirit. The resulting Elemental Gunblade is a masterwork of craftsmanship and arcane power, unique to you and unusable by anyone else.

Upon completing the ritual, you gain proficiency with your Elemental Gunblade, which retains the properties of both the original melee weapon and firearm. The elemental gunblade also counts as one of your chosen weapons and benefits from the +1 bonus to attack rolls.

Elemental Reverb
At 7th level, you gain the ability to instantly channel the full force of an Elemental Stance through your Gunblade. Once per short rest, as part of an attack, you can apply one of your known stance's max stack effect on your target.

Additionally, when you switch stances from max stacks, the energy release emits a 15-foot radius elemental shockwave, dealing 2d8 force damage and pushing creatures of your choice back 5 feet on a failed Dexterity save.

Stance Weaving
7rd-level Mysticshift Duelist feature

By 7th level, you have mastered the ability to shift between your known elemental stances in such rapid fluidity that they have begun to weave more effectively.

As a bonus action on your turn, you enter a perfect weave state for 1 minute. If you have a stance active, you gain 5 stacks in it immediately. While in this state, when you switch to a new stance the effects from the previous one linger until the next switch. You must also switch stances every turn to keep perfect weave active. You lose perfect weave at the end of your turn if you have not switched stances atleast once.

You may enter this state as many times as your proficiency bonus and uses recharge on a short rest.

Your body has the ability to recover quickly from terrible injuries, and is unusually receptive to healing magic. You gain the following benefits:
*  Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
*  When you are successfully stabilized while dying, you regain hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
*  Whenever you regain hit points as a result of a spell, potion, or class feature (but not this feat), you regain additional hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

A creature moving across the covered area must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. A creature moving through the area at half speed doesn't need to make the saving throw.

attribs.current:
As an action, you can splash the contents of this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a target creature, treating the holy water as an improvised weapon. If the target is a fiend or undead, it takes 2d6 radiant damage.

A cleric or paladin may create holy water by performing a special ritual. The ritual takes 1 hour to perform, uses 25 gp worth of powdered silver, and requires the caster to expend a 1st-level spell slot.

attribs.name: repeating_inventory_-Nzno3qk2keyHMmzVWZX_itemcontent
attribs.current: This lens allows a closer look at small objects. It is also useful as a substitute for flint and steel when starting fires. Lighting a fire with a magnifying glass requires light as bright as sunlight to focus, tinder to ignite, and about 5 minutes for the fire to ignite. A magnifying glass grants advantage on any ability check made to appraise or inspect an item that is small or highly detailed.

Breaking them requires a successful DC 20 Strength check. Each set of manacles comes with one key. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves' tools can pick the manacles' lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Manacles have 15 hit points.

attribs.name: repeating_spell-1_-O-NtzZEaPbbQN1v162A_spelldescription
attribs.current:
You place a curse on a creature that you can see within range. Until the spell ends, you deal an extra 1d6 necrotic damage to the target whenever you hit it with an attack. Also, choose one ability when you cast the spell. The target has disadvantage on ability checks made with the chosen ability.

If the target drops to 0 hit points before this spell ends, you can use a bonus action on a subsequent turn of yours to curse a new creature.

A remove curse cast on the target ends this spell early.

attribs.name: repeating_spell-1_-O-Ntztfh1pU2GVJGPXw_spellcomp_materials
attribs.current: holy water or powdered silver and iron, which the spell consumes

attribs.name: repeating_spell-1_-O-Ntztfh1pU2GVJGPXw_spelldescription
attribs.current:
Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch is protected against certain types of creatures: aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead.

The protection grants several benefits. Creatures of those types have disadvantage on attack rolls against the target. The target also can't be charmed, frightened, or possessed by them. If the target is already charmed, frightened, or possessed by such a creature, the target has advantage on any new saving throw against the relevant effect.

attribs.name: repeating_spell-cantrip_-O1ch-4EGsZ7hQnnvNuE_spelldescription
attribs.current:
As a part of casting this spell you touch a weapon or a piece of ammunition. A pungent poison trickles from your fingers, coating it. The next attack made with this weapon deals an additional 1d6 poisoned damage.

If no attack was made within the duration, the poison becomes inert and disappears.

At level 5, the extra poison damage dealt increases to 2d6, at level 11 the damage increases to 3d6 and at level 17 the damage increases to 4d6.

attribs.name: repeating_spell-cantrip_-O1chf-dVup2DPElOZGy_spelldescription
attribs.current:
You must be a humanoid possessing blood to cast this spell. You touch another humanoid possessing blood and siphon blood either into it or from it. Each turn after the spell is cast, the creature losing blood will lose 1d10 hipoints while the recipient will gain that amount.

If the creature is unwilling to transfer blood it must be grappled or restrained for this spell to work.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O1ciQlpoBkDREpP1gRo_description
attribs.current: Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail with a bonus equal to your fighter level. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O1ciocx9Rh7SWAaIeDZ_description
attribs.current:
You are a master of weapons. From 9th level, whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can choose any of the kinds of Mastery weapons you're using and replace the Mastery property of each with another Mastery property. For example, you could replace the Longsword's Sap property with the Push property.

These property changes apply only for you, not for others, and the changes end for you when you finish your next Long rest.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O3tBMs93lKevXvbksWC_description
attribs.current:
Your mastery over the elemental forces not only empowers your attacks but also fortifies your resolve and vitality. This mastery manifests in two key ways:

Defensive Harmony: You gain a bonus to all saving throws equal to half the number of stacks (rounded down) you have in any stance. This bonus reflects your heightened elemental awareness, enhancing your ability to evade or withstand harmful effects.
Elemental Transference: When you switch stances, the accumulated elemental energy rejuvenates you, healing you for an amount equal to the number of stacks in the previous stance before the switch. This healing represents the restorative power of the elements flowing through you, a reward for your strategic mastery over the elemental stances.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O67Udih2lyJ0WLf8aQD_description
attribs.current: At 11th level, you can attack three times whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
